events.factual_description: National Sawdust presents the Hildegard Commission Concert 2026 on Thursday, December 10, 2026 at 7:30 PM, with doors at 6:30 PM, as a seated performance in Brooklyn. The 2026 winners are che buford, Līva Blūma, Fjóla Evans and Maria-Eduarda Mendes Martin. National Sawdust's commission page states that each winner composes a new work in response to a distinct miniature illustration from Hildegard von Bingen's codices, with the images brought into the performance through projection or dynamic animation. The commissioned works are performed and recorded by Trinity Choir and the National Sawdust Ensemble with music direction by cellist Jeffrey Zeigler. National Sawdust lists sliding-scale tickets from $5 to $50. The individual event page contains a stale 'This event has passed' label, but the venue's current performances calendar lists the December 10 concert among upcoming performances and the authorized AudienceView/OvationTix ticket destination remains active.

enrichment.note: National Sawdust verifies the date, doors, showtime, seated format, $5–50 sliding scale, four 2026 winners, Trinity Choir, National Sawdust Ensemble, Jeffrey Zeigler and the Hildegard-image/projection concept. en.why_it_matters: Four new commissions are being built directly from Hildegard von Bingen's miniature images, then handed to Trinity Choir and the National Sawdust Ensemble inside a projected visual environment. That makes the concert more than an annual new-music showcase: the hook is hearing four composers translate the same medieval visual-spiritual source into different contemporary sound worlds at the moment the work enters public life.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already in play on December 10, I would build the Brooklyn evening around this concert. From the DMV, pair it with another strong New York reason rather than make a dedicated corridor trip for this date alone.

es.why_it_matters: Cuatro comisiones nuevas parten directamente de las miniaturas de Hildegard von Bingen y terminan en manos de Trinity Choir y National Sawdust Ensemble dentro de un entorno visual proyectado. Eso hace que la función sea más que una muestra anual de música nueva: lo que jala es escuchar cómo cuatro compositores traducen una misma fuente medieval, visual y espiritual, a lenguajes contemporáneos distintos justo cuando esas obras entran a la vida pública.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya está en juego el 10 de diciembre, armaría la noche de Brooklyn alrededor de este concierto. Desde el DMV, lo combinaría con otra razón fuerte para subir a Nueva York en vez de hacer un viaje regional dedicado únicamente por esta fecha.
